entries.title: Each article has a guide in Chat
entries.body: Each of your articles has a guide: a conversation pinned in Chat about how to read this piece and which modes suit it, whose greeting costs nothing until you write. Its answers carry buttons to open a mode or search, and when an answer finishes, the first button that only moves you, such as opening a Glossary already made, presses itself, while anything that spends or saves waits for you. On a wide screen, an article with no view remembered in this browser opens on the guide, not Summary.

entries.title: Ask a question on the Help pages
entries.body: Every Help page has an Ask about Spideryarn box: ask how to use the app and the answer, drawn from the Help pages, appears as it is written, with links only to Help pages. You need to be signed in. The Help pages also gain screenshots of the modes and short looping demonstrations of the strip showing where you are, Skim's steps and getting back after a jump, each with a still picture if your device asks for less motion.

entries.title: Adding an article you already have costs nothing
entries.body: Pasting the address of an article already in your library spends nothing; the add page says so and offers to open it. If you are signed in, someone else's public article offers to add a private copy to your library, where search and chat work, when its original address is known; a new copy uses one article allowance.

entries.title: Chat conversations are easier to move around in
entries.body: An open conversation has a labelled ‹ Chats button back to the list; its info card shows which AI answered, and how hard it thought. Long conversations in Chat and Learn gain first, previous and next message buttons. Dictation no longer shifts the buttons at Stop, and when the microphone you chose is no longer there, it goes straight to your default one instead of trying the missing one first.

entries.title: Controls doing the same job look the same
entries.body: Buttons, text boxes and sort controls share one look in every mode, and most failure messages now share one warning colour. A row of choices that scrolls sideways fades at the edge when more lies beyond it. The bottom bar is regrouped: Skim follows Structure, Summary and Diagram, then comes More, and Comments sits beside Marginalia.

entries.title: Your connected AI assistant can fetch sharing links
entries.body: An AI assistant you connect from your own computer can fetch a private sharing link for one of your articles, with your approval every time. The privacy page says the administrator's AI assistant may receive readers' account details and usage counts, but not what they read or wrote. A gift email can also include an article to start reading.

entries.title: Referee can ask the AI about hidden text
entries.body: In Referee's Hidden text panel, a button asks a more capable AI whether each hidden passage it flagged looks probably harmless or worth a look, and why. Only short excerpts are sent, not the article, and the opinions are not saved and never hide or reorder the findings. It is behind the Experimental features switch on your profile page.

entries.title: Blog comments, Illustrated and rotation bugs fixed
entries.body: A short blog post could be added as its comments instead of the post; WordPress, Blogger and Disqus comment threads are set aside first. In Illustrated, one picture that timed out could end the whole set early; now only that picture fails and the rest carry on. Rotating a phone or tablet can no longer leave the page wider than the screen.
